note: The six load scenarios TEST_STRATEGY.md names, written out concretely: what is driven, at what rate, against what, and what result fails. Every rate here is derived from a policy default or from the private-beta population rather than chosen, and scripts/repository/validate_load_scenarios.py resolves each derivation against packages/schemas/policy-defaults-v1.json so a scenario cannot drift away from the contract it claims to come from.
claim_note: No scenario has been written as a k6 script and none has been run. This file is the specification, not evidence. A scenario listed here is a scenario somebody has to build, and an unrun scenario proves nothing about the system.

population.derivation: D-180 bounds the private beta by the number of invite codes the owner issues by hand, and packages/schemas/policy-defaults-v1.json sets invite_outstanding_max to 200. The ring size is therefore a row count rather than a chosen figure, and docs/architecture/API_EDGE_CONTRACT.md derives every rate limit from the same 200.

scale_target_note: None of these scenarios says anything about the 100,000 ranked-identity scale target. They are sized at 200 because that is the private beta, and passing at 200 demonstrates nothing at 100,000. D-094 recorded the ceiling, the scale target and the recovery objectives as an unresolved three-way conflict; D-360 resolved it by amending the ceiling to the measured steady-state cost of the selected configuration, leaving the scale target and the recovery objectives unchanged. So the tension a load test would have had to navigate is gone, and the reason not to write a 100,000-participant scenario is unchanged and simpler: nothing has measured that figure, and a scenario asserting it would be a number this repository invented.

execution.driver_licence: AGPL-3.0, invoked as a separate process and never linked into a distributed artifact; see docs/verification/TEST_STRATEGY.md
execution.target: a ci-provisioned ephemeral stack sized to match the production configuration selected under D-361, never production itself
execution.cadence: manually dispatched before each ring expansion of the private beta and before public launch; never per pull request
execution.recording: docs/verification/BENCHMARK_AND_EVIDENCE_PROTOCOLS.md metadata is mandatory: runner class, operating system, toolchain versions, dataset version, warmup policy, sample count, statistical summary and commit SHA. A result without it is not evidence.
execution.data: synthetic only, from evals/fixtures/ and conformance/, with no exception in any environment

beta-steady.intent: the load the private beta actually generates, held long enough for aggregate freshness to matter

operations.name: claim-batch-submit
operations.derivation: 200 devices x 1 batch per 60 s, the steady rate rate_limit_claim_ingest_per_minute is set at six times

operations.name: leaderboard-read
operations.derivation: 200 clients x 1 per public_cache_stale_seconds, because anything faster is a cache hit and never reaches the origin

beta-steady.fails_when: any p95 exceeds its bound, any 5xx is returned, or aggregate freshness exceeds 90 s at any point during the run rather than only at the end

beta-peak.intent: the aggregate admission ceiling, driven deliberately, to see what the edge does at its own limit

operations.name: beta-steady-mix-at-10x
operations.derivation: 10 x beta-steady, which is exactly aggregate_admission_ceiling_rps

beta-peak.fails_when: a request is refused with anything other than 429 plus Retry-After, a 5xx appears below the ceiling, or aggregate freshness has not returned to the beta-steady bound within 5 minutes of the peak ending. Requests refused at the ceiling itself return 503 with Retry-After, which is a statement about the service rather than about the client, and are counted separately from the 429s.

offline-drain.intent: the case where duplicate admission and exact idempotent replay are actually exercised at scale

operations.name: queued-backlog-drain
operations.derivation: 50 devices reconnecting at once, each carrying 24 h of queued minutes: 1,440 rows in three batches under batch_max_claims = 500. rate_limit_claim_ingest_per_minute permits 6 batches per minute per device, so a legitimate reconnect is never delayed by the limit.

operations.name: replayed-batches
operations.derivation: one in five batches is re-sent with an identical Idempotency-Key and identical bytes, and one in twenty with the same key and different bytes, per the idempotency contract in docs/architecture/API_EDGE_CONTRACT.md

offline-drain.fails_when: any claim is admitted twice, a byte-identical replay returns a non-identical response, a same-key-different-bytes request is accepted instead of refused, the drain exceeds 10 minutes, or a principal not participating in the drain sees latency degrade by more than half. SR-012 is open and the persistence half of exact replay is unrepaired, so this scenario is expected to fail until that closes; that expected failure is the point of writing it down.

leaderboard-thunder.intent: the shape of an announcement, which is the only load event that arrives without any enrolled device behind it

operations.name: unauthenticated-global-board-read
operations.derivation: 2,000 unauthenticated readers arriving within 60 s against the global board, which is the only view universally public by default

leaderboard-thunder.fails_when: origin request rate exceeds 60 per second, which would mean the public_cache_stale_seconds cache is not absorbing what it is sized to absorb; or read p95 exceeds 300 ms; or the connection pool is exhausted at any point

ratelimit-breach.intent: the only scenario that asserts a limit protects the people it exists for, rather than merely refusing someone

operations.name: breaching-principal
operations.derivation: one principal at 10 x rate_limit_authenticated_read_per_minute, which is 1,200 per minute against a quota of 120

operations.name: beta-steady-background
operations.derivation: beta-steady, unchanged, running concurrently so there is something to protect

ratelimit-breach.fails_when: the breaching principal is refused by anything other than 429 with a correct Retry-After, or any other principal's latency or error rate moves measurably. A limiter that sheds load onto bystanders has failed even when it correctly refused the abuser.

soak.intent: the failures that only appear on the time axis, which no throughput number finds
soak.fails_when: resident memory grows by more than a tenth, goroutines or pooled connections grow monotonically, or any table outside the append-only claim ledger grows without bound. Growth in the ledger is the product working; growth anywhere else is a leak.
